page: Microsoft Azure D16ls_v7 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D16ls_v7 demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, particularly in data compression and decompression tasks. Gzip compression single-threaded throughput reaches 35.31 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression single-threaded throughput is measured at 14.95 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier performance in text generation using a small 135M model, delivering 350.22 tokens/sec. Other metrics, such as the stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 18136.46, PassMark CPU score of 30370.06, and Redis SET operations at 31.34 million operations per second, fall within the average range.

The primary tradeoff of the D16ls_v7 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external network-attached storage. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not demand large memory footprints or local disk space. It is suited for tasks such as single-threaded data processing, web serving, lightweight machine learning inference, and general compute tasks that leverage advanced vector and matrix extensions like AVX-512 and AMX.
